e: Colombia severs relations with Iran, alleging that the Iranian government has connections to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the country's security."
President de la Espriella deploys the army to Santa Marta following a series of attacks in the city blamed on the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada.

Colombia–United States relations: The United States and Colombia sign a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals and rare earths during a visit by US secretary of state Marco Rubio to Barranquilla.
President de la Espriella signs a decree lifting the nationwide suspension of permits to carry firearms that had been in place since 2015.
Naín Andrés Pérez Toncel aka "Bendito Menor", a leader of the armed group Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada, is killed in a security operation in Riohacha.
A car bomb explodes near a police station in Los Patios, killing one and injuring 11.
The lifting of reciprocal visa requirements between Colombia and Israel comes into effect.
Viviane Morales resigns as education minister effective 7 September, citing personal reasons. She is replaced by Ilva Myriam Hoyos.
At least 20 FARC dissidents are reported killed in an airstrike in Guaviare Department.
President de la Espriella formally ends negotiations under the Petro administration's Total Peace policy.
An unlicensed gold mine collapses in Nariño Department, killing 13 workers and injuring seven others.
Congress elects Jorge Eliécer Laverde Vargas as Comptroller General.
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake hits Chocó Department, killing 331 people.
Colombia recognizes Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.
Two security guards are injured in a bomb attack on a tollbooth in Cauca Department.
Abelardo de la Espriella is inaugurated as president in a ceremony in Cali.
A truck bomb explodes near the Norte de Santander Police Command in Cúcuta, injuring 11 officers and killing a service dog.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Colombia, citing the presence of alleged forced labor in the supply chain.
The ELN release two police officers held captive in Arauca Department since 2025.
The ELN declares a unilateral ceasefire from 20 to 23 June to allow for the holding of the 2026 Colombian presidential election on 21 June.
At least seven people are killed in territorial clashes between the Misak and Nasa indigenous groups in Silvia, Cauca.
Former Cubarral mayor Rogers Devia and his staffer are shot dead amid campaigning for the presidential election.
Nine people are killed in a gas explosion at a coal mine in Sutatausa.
Three people are killed and at least 38 are injured when a monster truck crashes into spectators during a stunt performance at a public exhibition in Popayán.
The First Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels is held in Santa Marta.
Three soldiers are killed in drone strikes carried out by the rebel group Comandos de la Frontera in Ipiales.
President Petro accuses Ecuador of infiltrating its territory and carrying out an airstrike that killed 27 people along their border.
Authorities announce the arrest of 121 people in a nationwide operation against criminal groups and the ELN.
The ELN declares a unilateral ceasefire to allow for the holding of the 2026 Colombian parliamentary election on 8 March.

The Search Unit for Disappeared Persons announces the discovery and identification of the remains of Catholic priest turned ELN leadzer Camilo Torres Restrepo, who was killed fighting the military in 1966.
President Petro announces that he had survived an assassination attempt along with his daughters aboard a helicopter.
Senator Aida Quilcué and two bodyguards are briefly abducted from their vehicle in Cauca Department.
At least 22 people are reported killed in flooding across four northern departments.
Two people are killed while four others are reported missing following an ambush on a convoy of senator Jairo Castellanos in Arauca Department.
The United Kingdom imposes sanctions on three Colombians accused of recruiting mercenaries for the Rapid Support Forces in the Sudanese civil war (2023–present).
Santiago Gallon Henao, a suspect in the 1994 killing of football player Andrés Escobar, is shot dead in Mexico.
Six people are killed in a methane explosion at the Mata Siete coal mine in Guachetá.
Seven ELN rebels are killed in a military operation near the Venezuelan border.
The government issues a decree restricting the importation of drones, citing their usage in attacks by armed anti-state forces.

Colombia announces a 30% tariff on unspecified imports from Ecuador and suspends sales of electricity to the latter country in retaliation for Quito imposing a 30% tariff on Colombian goods the previous day.
